subject: DPA: international transfer carveouts & MSA order form tie-in
messages:
From: Natalie Kumar <natalie.kumar@datahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@datahealth.com
Date: 2025-11-17T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA redline + SCCs mapping (initial pass)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for walking through the overall MSA/order form last week. Attached is our redline of Redwood's standard DPA (DataHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx) plus an annotated SCCs role mapping (SCCs_role_mapping_annotated.xlsx) that highlights where we need clarification on processor vs controller responsibilities for cross-border flows.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept the carveout language in section 5.2 for EU->US transfers (we included two alternatives).
- Can you provide a short write-up on the practical subprocessor list/update cadence for regulatory audits? We need this for our internal privacy evidencing.
- Please confirm whether the Order Form will include the new clause tying export-control contact points to the DPA (we suggested wording in the exhibit).

We'd like to avoid protracted redlines — if you can indicate which items are non-starters for Redwood by EOD Wednesday (11/19), we can prepare a targeted escalation channel on our side.

Attachments: DataHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx (redline), SCCs_role_mapping_annotated.xlsx (annotated)

Best,
Natalie Kumar
Head of Legal Ops
DataHealth Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Kumar <natalie.kumar@datahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCCs mapping (initial pass)

Natalie —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Quick responses inline: 

- Carveout language (section 5.2): We can accept Alternative B from your draft with a small clarification to preserve our fallback routing policy for customers in regulated sectors. I pasted suggested language below — happy to discuss: "Where applicable, Redwood will route processing to an approved region or fallback model variant where required by local regulation; Redwood will document such routing in the Order Form."

- Subprocessor cadence: we publish a rolling subprocessor registry and maintain a 30-day advance notice for material additions. For audit evidence we can provide an expiring delta export (CSV) per your request and certify lists on a quarterly cadence.

- Order Form export-control contact tie-in: OK in principle. We propose a 1-sentence exhibit linking the named contact and the DPA effective date; see Exhibit H in our attached template.

Ben and Karthik — can you weigh in on whether the fallback routing sentence above is acceptable operationally? If not, call out constraints and I'll feed them back to DataHealth.

Next steps: I'll coordinate an internal review with Legal infra and send back a consolidated set of comments by EOD 11/19. If there are open high-risk items after that, propose a 30-minute triage call.

Best,
Marissa
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-18T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline + SCCs mapping (internal ops review)

Marissa — forwarding my notes after a quick ops sync with Karthik and Jordan. 

On the fallback routing sentence: operationally feasible but need to clarify scope — specifically whether routing is per-tenant or per-request. We can support tenant-level routing via Order Form flags. Per-request routing adds latency and requires a model-variant cache warmup; that's a non-trivial engineering change with an estimated uplift in 99th percentile latency for affected requests. 

Proposed compromise language for the DPA: "Fallback routing will be applied at the tenancy level as specified in the Order Form; ad-hoc per-request routing is subject to engineering review and a mutually-agreed implementation timeline."

On subprocessor evidence: we can produce the quarterly certified list plus a one-off export for procurement/ audit requests. For continuous evidence, we can offer a time-limited secure CSV export (DRS) as Marissa suggested.

Attachments referenced: None (we reviewed DataHealth files in drive).

Ben Carter
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Natalie Kumar <natalie.kumar@datahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@datahealth.com, tom.reyes@datahealth.com
Date: 2025-11-20T15:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCCs mapping (next steps + call invite)

Marissa / Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and for surfacing the operational constraints. The wording Ben proposed is acceptable to DataHealth with one small edit (we want explicit mention that Order Form flags are binding for the lifecycle of the relationship). Final proposed sentence: 

"Fallback routing will be applied at the tenancy level as specified in the Order Form and will be binding for the duration of the Agreement; ad-hoc per-request routing is subject to engineering review and a mutually-agreed implementation timeline."

On subprocessor evidence: that approach works. Could you please: 
1) Share a draft CSV export schema so our compliance team can confirm it meets audit requirements (we flagged required fields in the attached SCCs spreadsheet).
2) Add an Exhibit H entry showing the named export-control contact and a sample Order Form snippet.

We have a hard internal deadline to complete legal sign-off by 11/25. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow (11/21) at 10:00 AM CET to finalize the two outstanding bullets above? I've attached a proposed short agenda and included a DocuSign link for the MSA redline in case the commercial team approves the non-substantive redlines today.

Attachments: DPA_redline_summary.pdf (one-page), SCCs_role_mapping_annotated.xlsx (referenced)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/12345-DataHealth-DPA

Best,
Natalie Kumar
Head of Legal Ops
DataHealth Inc.
